title: A regularization method for quantum neural networks using data symmetry
abstract: Leveraging data symmetries has recently become a key strategy in quantum neural networks (QNNs) to improve generalization and training efficiency. In this study, we propose a novel regularization method for QNNs based on input data symmetry. By introducing a penalty term that encourages the model to align with data symmetry, our method enables improved training speed and generalization. This symmetry-based regularization is simple to implement and does not require prior knowledge of the symmetry group. We validate its effectiveness through numerical experiments on both classification tasks and quantum generative adversarial networks. Empirical results demonstrate faster convergence and lower test errors. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical generalization bound using Rademacher complexity and conjecture a condition under which models with symmetry exhibit better generalization. Our findings highlight the potential of symmetry-aware regularization in enhancing the performance of QML models.
summary: This paper introduces a novel regularization technique for Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) that leverages the inherent symmetries of the input data. By adding a symmetry-preserving penalty term to the loss function, the method improves training speed and generalization performance across various tasks. The results demonstrate that incorporating this symmetry knowledge enhances QML model robustness.
main_problem: The study aims to improve the generalization performance and accelerate the training speed of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) by incorporating constraints derived from input data symmetries.
main_result: The proposed symmetry-based regularization method leads to faster convergence and lower test errors across both classification tasks and quantum generative adversarial networks compared to unregularized models. Theoretically, it provides a generalization bound suggesting improved performance when symmetry is enforced.
method: A novel penalty term, $C_{	ext{symm}}$, is added to the cost function, forcing the parameterized quantum circuit's unitary evolution to align with the symmetries inherent in the input data density matrix $ho_{in}(x)$. Theoretical analysis involves deriving Rademacher complexity bounds.
model_or_system: The model utilizes QNNs implemented via parameterized quantum circuits $U(	heta)$, whose output is measured as an expectation value. The analysis covers both classification tasks and generative modeling using Quantum GANs, requiring the definition of input density matrices $ho_{in}(x)$ for different scenarios.
key_observables: Test errors, convergence speed, Frobenius norm ($\lVert S U(	heta) S^\dagger - U(	heta) Vert_F$), and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for generative tasks.
important_parameters: The balancing parameter $C$ controlling the regularization strength; circuit depth ($d=2, d=4$).
main_assumptions: It is assumed that enforcing data symmetry via a penalty term can constrain the search space beneficially without overly restricting expressibility. A key limitation noted is that generative tasks might show instability with strong symmetry constraints.
figures_summary: Figures compare loss results for classification (varying depth and regularization strength $C$) and show FID scores for generative tasks up to 100 iterations, illustrating the impact of the penalty term.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the symmetry-based regularization method using data symmetries ($ho_{in}(x)$), provides theoretical generalization bounds via Rademacher complexity, and validates the approach through numerical experiments on both classification and QGAN tasks.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical challenges in quantum machine learning by providing a principled way to regularize models based on underlying physical symmetries, which is crucial for building robust quantum algorithms.
